extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers interested in philosophy of religion and science
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical treatment arguing how Religion and Science should be understood as complementary and how to find their common ground; includes methodological guidance about concept-formation and legitimate kinds of religious/scientific claims. Intended as a chapter-length analytic exposition rather than a technical paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability of science (verification and criticism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science is substantially true because its propositions have been subjected to rigorous criticism over generations, errors are mercilessly exposed, and scientific predictions are daily verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the long history of intersubjective criticism, mutual examination by scientists, and continual empirical verification (including technological successes) as grounds for treating scientific claims as reliable. Failures or shortcomings of individual advocates do not impugn the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge science by its methods, not its advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-comings in the advocates do not tell essentially against that which is advocated; Science must be judged by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between the character or faults of proponents and the merits of the scientific claims and methods; avoid dismissing scientific conclusions on the basis of imperfect defenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to verify and to receive verified truth with humility
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the duty of every one to verify scientific disclosures as far as in him lies; and having verified, to receive with all humility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages individual effort to test or understand scientific claims personally when possible, and to accept verified conclusions modestly rather than resist them on prior belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Both Religion and Science contain genuine truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion, pervasive in human history, expresses some eternal fact; Science is an organised, ever-growing mass of facts being purified from errors. If both have bases in reality, there must be a fundamental harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach the apparent conflict assuming both domains can express aspects of truth; avoid framing the relation as absolute opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual recognition and impartial study of the other
rubrics_metrics.description: Each side must recognize the claims of the other as standing for truths not to be ignored; the religious must see Science as a constituent of the whole, and the scientific must learn to treat Religion as a subject of science with no more prejudice than any other reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate sympathetic and impartial study: each tradition should strive to understand the other, presuming that the other has something worthy to be understood and that mutual recognition will enable reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek the most abstract common ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Only some highly abstract proposition can serve as the desired basis of agreement; neither particular dogmas nor specific scientific doctrines can become Religious conceptions. The common ground must be the most abstract element in both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In attempting reconciliation, look for general, highly abstract truths (the elements common to all religions and the root facts underlying all sciences) rather than trying to reconcile particular doctrines or branch-specific scientific claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for a real and permanent reconciliation, not makeshift compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not reconcile them in any makeshift way or temporary compromise; seek that intimate truth which both will avow with absolute sincerity and without mental reservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject artificial compromises that both parties privately regard as temporary; pursue a synthesis in which the common ground is genuinely maintained by both sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate opposed convictions to produce higher development
rubrics_metrics.description: From the coalescence of antagonist ideas, each containing its portion of truth, there arises a higher development. Examples: synthesis in geology, biology, psychology, sociology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical examples of intellectual synthesis to motivate efforts to combine religious and scientific perspectives; expect that coordination will yield novel insights and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy criterion for symbolic conceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many general conceptions are symbolic (inadequate representatives). Such symbolic conceptions are legitimate provided that by cumulative or indirect thought processes, or by fulfilment of predictions based on them, we can assure ourselves they stand for actualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat symbolic or abstract notions as acceptable only when they are amenable to indirect verification (e.g., predictive success, measurable consequences) or can be expanded into adequate conceptions by further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject unverifiable symbolic conceptions as vicious
rubrics_metrics.description: When symbolic conceptions are such that no cumulative or indirect processes of thought can ascertain corresponding actualities, nor can any predictions be made whose fulfilment can prove them, then they are altogether vicious and elusive and indistinguishable from pure fictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid building reconciliations or religious doctrines on symbolic ideas that cannot in principle be tested or connected to experience; these are epistemically worthless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware the gradual slide from concrete to deceptive symbolic thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an insensible transition from actual conceptions to symbolic ones; we habitually mistake symbolic conceptions for real ones and are led into countless false inferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain critical awareness of where conceptual representation becomes inadequate (as scale, complexity, or plurality increases) and avoid treating inadequate symbolic representations as full understandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological humility about ultimate cosmological explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Common cosmogonic hypotheses (self-existence, self-creation, creation by external agency) may be verbally intelligible but are shown to be inconceivable upon critical examination; conceivability matters, not mere verbal plausibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating ultimate explanations (origins of the universe), require conceptual coherency and conceivability; don't accept hypotheses that rest on notions (like existence without beginning, potential becoming actual without cause, creation of space) that cannot be coherently represented in thought.
